summary: This survey covers institution-level enrollment and instructional activity delivered from July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, for undergraduate and graduate education. It reports activity over the full 12-month period, including institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs, rather than a single term. The universe is institutions reporting undergraduate or graduate enrollment or instructional activity; the enrollment table uses institution and enrollment level as its reporting unit.

Fall Enrollment tables report aggregate counts or institution-level measures for participating postsecondary institutions, with the institution as the reporting unit rather than individual student records. Traditional academic-year institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date; institutions with program-specific or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. The tables cover institutions and students eligible for the applicable Fall Enrollment reporting, with some measures restricted to particular institution types or student populations as noted below.

The Finance survey collects institutional financial data during the winter collection period following the fiscal year, covering each institution’s fiscal year ending in the reporting year; reporting is annual and required for eligible Title IV postsecondary institutions. The unit of observation is the institution, identified by UNITID, and the universe is eligible postsecondary institutions that were open and operating during the fiscal year. Finance reporting is separated by institutional sector and accounting model, so the applicable table depends on whether the institution uses GASB or FASB and whether it is public, private not-for-profit, or private for-profit.

The Graduation Rates survey is collected annually during the July 1–November 24 collection window and reports cohort outcomes as of August 31 of the reporting year. Its unit of observation is the institution and its full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate cohorts; it applies to eligible institutions that enroll such students and reports enrollment, completion, and transfer status. Cohorts and measures are separated by institution level and the applicable normal-time interval, so coverage varies by institution type and cohort.

Human Resources data cover institution-level staff and employee reporting for fall, generally as of November 1, plus academic-year salary and fringe-benefit reporting. Institutions may have multiple records, with UNITID combined with table-specific classification fields defining each record; coverage includes eligible postsecondary institutions and related administrative offices, subject to the restrictions stated for individual tables. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years for the applicable HR tables, so 2010 (even) may have no data for those breakdowns.

Institutional Characteristics is collected in the fall for the 2010-11 academic year, with institutions reporting institution- or campus-level information for the applicable reporting period, generally as of October 1, 2010. The universe is the active IPEDS postsecondary institution universe, including Title IV-participating institutions for which reporting is mandatory and other eligible institutions that may report voluntarily. Institutions may be represented through parent/child or multi-campus reporting arrangements, and not every item applies to every institution.

The Student Financial Aid survey covers aid received from July 1, 2009, through June 30, 2010, reported at the institution level. It concerns undergraduate students at IPEDS institutions, with the detailed populations and eligibility varying by table; the survey is useful for examining aid recipients, aid amounts, and net price rather than institution-wide financial aid for all students.
